nodes.description: Season table, one row per player and team of ACB 2025-2026; traded players also carry a `team_name = 'total'` row with a null `team_id`.
Season table, one row per player and team of ACB 2025-2026; traded players also carry a `team_name = 'total'` row with a null `team_id`.
Season table, one row per player and team of ACB 2025-2026; traded players also carry a `team_name = 'total'` row with a null `team_id`.
One row per player in a chance: the shot location and the rebound location, with no frames of its own. Conformed into silver `events` as `chance_players`.
One row per chance, a stretch of a possession from its start to its end frame, with the start type, the outcome and where it ended.
One row per closeout: the ball handler, the defender who closes out on them, and the start and end locations.
One row per dribble: the ball handler, the frame and the location.
One row per drive: the ball handler, the defender on them, the start and end frames and the start and end locations.
One row per foul: the fouler and their team, the fouled player, the frame and the location.
Conformed as `shot`; native_family keeps them apart from open play.
One row per handoff: the setter, the receiver, the frame and the location.
One row per isolation: the ball handler, their defender, the start and end frames and locations.
One row per matchup: the offensive player, the defender assigned to them and the start and end frames. No location or outcome.
One row per off-ball screen: the cutter, the screener, the frame and the location.
A family of its own here; football has no equivalent event and marks a pass on how a player_possession ended.
One row per pick: the ball handler, the screener, the frame and the location.
The native team possession, and the carrier of `leftHoop`: every other family rotates its coordinates by the one its `possessionId` points at.
One row per post-up: the ball handler, their defender, the start and end frames and locations, and the section of the court.
One row per rebound: the rebounder, their team, the frame, the location and whether it was defensive.
`location` is where the provider says the shot happened, not where the shooter stood at `startFrame` (task 9).
One row per timeout: the team that called it and the frame. No player, location or outcome.
One player holding the ball. Conformed as `player_possession`.
One row per turnover: the player who turned the ball over, the player who stole it, the frame and the location.
One row per player and match, both benches included.
One row per match, folded from game_data.json: the match header, with the same file read once for this table and game_players.
One row per match of the ACB season bundle; the only place with the score.
Season table. Some rows map a duplicated player id onto its canonical one. It never rewrites an id in silver (decision 4): it fills dim_entity.canonical_player_id and gold applies it.
One row per frame, timeouts included. dim_period reads its period boundaries from here because game_data.json does not publish them.

One row per frame and object, the ball included as a side of its own. A timeout frame has no row here at all, which is why `frames` loses about 44% of the basketball file and keeps the timeline in bronze.
Task 9's probe: the sign of the attack per (match, period, team) and the court.
Season table, one row per player, team and `position_group` of the A-League 2024/2025 (not per player and team: that pair repeats).
Season table, one row per player, team and `position_group` of the A-League 2024/2025 (not per player and team: that pair repeats).
Season table, one row per player, team and `position_group` of the A-League 2024/2025 (not per player and team: that pair repeats).
One row per line of the body pose file, in the file's own frame numbering, with the number of players in the frame. Frames outside every period have no players.
One row per frame and player that has a pose: 29 joints in metres and their error. A player with no pose has no row; the count of players stays in bodypose_frames.

The four native event types in one CSV of frozen columns: player_possession, passing_option, on_ball_engagement and off_ball_run. Its `first_player_possession_in_team_possession` flag is the provider delimiting its own team possessions, which is the rule `events` uses.
One row per match, folded from match.json. Carries the score, the pitch (which is not the same in every match: its length varies) and the competition edition.
One row per match and period, with the frame the period starts and ends at.
One row per player and match. `id` is the key the tracking uses (`tracking_objects.player_id`), not `trackable_object`.
Season table written as a single file, one row per match of the A-League 2024/2025 bundle, each row carrying its own `match_id`.
One row per phase of play. A phase is not a team possession: many carry `team_possession_loss_in_phase`, which is why the chain rule won over merging them.
One row per frame, the ball among its columns rather than as an object. Frames outside every period carry a null period, no player and no ball.
One row per frame and player; the ball is not here, it is in tracking_frames.

Basketball season aggregate `aggregates_drives` as bronze wrote it, without `source_file` and `source_row`, plus `is_season_total`. Grain: one row per (player_id, team_id); traded players also carry a `team_name = 'total'` row with a null `team_id` (`is_season_total`).

Basketball season aggregate `aggregates_picks` as bronze wrote it, without `source_file` and `source_row`, plus `is_season_total`. Grain: one row per (player_id, team_id); traded players also carry a `team_name = 'total'` row with a null `team_id` (`is_season_total`).

Basketball season aggregate `aggregates_shots` as bronze wrote it, without `source_file` and `source_row`, plus `is_season_total`. Grain: one row per (player_id, team_id); traded players also carry a `team_name = 'total'` row with a null `team_id` (`is_season_total`).

Football season aggregate `aggregates_obr` as bronze wrote it, without `source_file` and `source_row`, plus `is_season_total`. Grain: one row per (player_id, team_id, position_group); the (player, team) pair repeats once per `position_group`, so the key has three columns.

Football season aggregate `aggregates_passing` as bronze wrote it, without `source_file` and `source_row`, plus `is_season_total`. Grain: one row per (player_id, team_id, position_group); the (player, team) pair repeats once per `position_group`, so the key has three columns.

Football season aggregate `aggregates_physical` as bronze wrote it, without `source_file` and `source_row`, plus `is_season_total`. Grain: one row per (player_id, team_id, position_group); the (player, team) pair repeats once per `position_group`, so the key has three columns.
One row per (sport, family, metric) with at least one non-null value; `kind` is read off the name.
One row per player and sport across the six aggregates, with the provider's own id.
One row per team and sport in the six aggregates. Not called `dim_team` because silver already has one; the season-total row of a traded player is not a team.
One row per non-null numeric cell of the six aggregates. Rows with `is_season_total` are the provider's totals of traded players: filter them out before summing.
manifest/sources.json: each source's repo, pinned commit, files and sha256.
reports/pose_coverage.json: frames, player-frames and joints with a pose per match, checked.
reports/pose_metric.json: the metric in both matches, recomputed and compared.
reports/pose_protocol.json: the frozen protocol against the code and the denominators.
web/public/data/pose.json and pose/*.json, regenerated and compared.
6 curated possessions per sport, written to web/public/data/possessions/.
web/public/data/quality.json and docs/bulletin.md, from reports/quality_*.csv.
web/public/data/runs.json and runs/*.json, regenerated and compared.
web/public/data/stats.json: rows per table and sport, raw and published bytes.
Whether the clock is exact: the step between two native frames, per match.
How often the provider says it saw each kind of object, per match.
Entry angle of a made shot: what the bundle reports against the geometry.
Apparent gravity of the ball per match: the g its free flights fall with.
Frame-to-frame jitter of the ball against detected players, both sports.
The partitions no field in either bundle declares, one row per match.
opendata-basketball, every manifest file with the right sha256.
opendata-football, every manifest file with the right sha256.
opendata-bodypose, every manifest file with the right sha256.
Task 9's probe: the sign of the attack per (match, period, team) and the court.
Task 9's probe: the sign of the attack per (match, period, team) and the court.
reports/runs_coverage.csv: runs, windows and placebos per match, checked.
reports/runs_calibration.json, section effect (M3 to M5a), recomputed and compared.
reports/runs_calibration.json, section probe (M1, M2), recomputed and compared.
reports/runs_protocol.json: the split, the windows and the death criteria, checked.

The conformed vocabulary, one row per (sport, native family, subtype pattern). A row with a literal subtype wins over the `*` of its family, which is how a football player_possession that ended in a pass becomes a `pass` while the rest stay `player_possession`.

The surface specs a match can be played on, with their dimensions in metres. Two rows: the FIBA court task 9 measured, and the NBA court it rejected, kept so the rejection stays visible instead of disappearing into a WHERE clause. Football does not appear here because its pitch is declared per match by the provider.
Everything that can hold a position in a match: both benches and the ball. Built from the roster, which covers every id the tracking uses in both sports and also the players who never left the bench.
One row per match, 20 in total, with the surface, the periods and the pinned commit.
One row per match and period. Football declares its boundaries in match.json; basketball's are read off the tracking, which is the only place its period changes.

The two rows that turn `sport` into a column. Every constant of a bundle that silver needs lives here once: the unit and its factor to metres, the sample rate, the semantics of the official clock, how many players are on the surface and which frame the provider's events arrive in.
One row per team, 30 in total (17 basketball, 13 football).
Task 9 in silver keys: which way each team attacks in each period, and the evidence that fixed it. Two rows per (match, period), opposite signs, asserted by tests/assert_attack_signs_opposite.sql.

Every event of both bundles in one shape: 20 native families in basketball, 4 plus the phases of play in football, and the football team possession this project derives. Coordinates are rotated to the venue frame, and a row whose rotation cannot be resolved carries none.
Which team possession a frame belongs to. A view, because expanding the possessions to their frames would write tens of millions of rows that are one range join away from what silver already holds.

The physical record of both sports in one shape: one row per match, native frame and entity, in metres and in the venue frame. Built from the tracking and from nothing else. Partitioned on disk by sport and native match id, because a silver match_id carries a colon and that is not a directory name on Windows.

The frames of a team possession, turned so the team with the ball attacks towards +x: x_att_m = attack_sign * x_m. The only attack normalisation in silver. A frame no possession claims is absent, never given a guessed sign.
